Is there any reason why replicate_succ is not discoverable by simp and only by grind? I was looking at the code base here:

@[simp, grind =] theorem replicate_zero {a : α} : replicate 0 a = [] := rfl
@[grind =] theorem replicate_succ {a : α} {n : Nat} : replicate (n+1) a = a :: replicate n a := rfl

and oddly simp can discover almost all the theorems but not this one. Maybe this creates some conflict in the order of simp searching?
It has a twice on the right hand side, which may not be desired if a is a big expression. Not sure why it's fine for grind
Well, a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: [] isn't exactly simpler than replicate 10 a, is it? simp is supposed to make things simpler, not longer.

Ruben Van de Velde said:

It has a twice on the right hand side, which may not be desired if a is a big expression. Not sure why it's fine for grind

expressions occurring twice do not double term size in grins but only add constant overhead

Ruben Van de Velde said:

It has a twice on the right hand side, which may not be desired if a is a big expression. Not sure why it's fine for grind

So far I could say the same for f in something like

@[simp, grind =] theorem map_cons {f : α → β} {a : α} {l : List α} : map f (a :: l) = f a :: map f l := rfl

and yet it allows factoring out the first item just fine while also being simp annotated.

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

Well, a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: a :: [] isn't exactly simpler than replicate 10 a, is it? simp is supposed to make things simpler, not longer.

Not sure how you evaluate complexity here but I would not take the length of an expression as a strict complexity metric even though I understand you grounding in human cognition.

I think the difference here is that you don't want things to blow up if someone writes replicate 1000000 a. But there is no easy analogous way to blow up the map_cons. In grind it doesn't blow up because grind only does a handful of rewrite iterations, while simp needs to repeat it 1000000 times.

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

I think the difference here is that you don't want things to blow up if someone writes replicate 1000000 a. But there is no easy analogous way to blow up the map_cons. In grind it doesn't blow up because grind only does a handful of rewrite iterations, while simp needs to repeat it 1000000 times.

I think I get your point here but maybe simp could be improved to max out much faster since I doubt there will be a practical proof ever needed by humans where one would need to apply replicate_succ a million times. This could then make simp more resilient and allow for automatic discovery of more theorems and prevent unnatural cases where certain cons theorems are easily discoverable while others are not simply because a human has shorthand notation to blow things up. I assume people are already taking such extra steps on the grind side which is why it already has a greater reach than simp.
